My name is not important, but I am a woman of 47 years here in Machinga, and this small maize garden of mine feeds my household. I will try to get a little fertilizer through the subsidy coupon if I am lucky this year — without it, the soil here is too tired to give good maize. I keep some chickens and a goat so I carry their droppings to the field, and I plant pigeon peas together with the maize as my mother taught me. Seed is expensive, so I buy one small packet of hybrid from the trading centre and keep some local seed from last year as backup; for the armyworm I only scout and crush them by hand because chemicals cost too much, and rain is what waters my field — I have no pump, no river close by.
